title: Ai for pixelart
author: Chonki_Chonga
selftext: What ai do you guys use for pixelart of small models. 16-50 pixels are my characters

comments.author: jasontlouro
comments.body:
I use a custom system that actually uses text models. Currently using GPT 6.1 terra. For tiles it generates a spec for each tile using combinations of textures/patterns that it then renders with a color palette. For sprites it generates a 'skeleton', rigs it for the various animations, then applies a color palette and renders it. 

Here is one example of an animated sprite

replies.author: KingManon
replies.body: Can you say more about this “custom system”? Can it make proper walking frames of people?

replies.author: jasontlouro
replies.body:
For anything that moves, a text model is prompted to write a JSON document in a specific format that encodes bones/rigging, shapes attached to those bones and the colors associated with those shapes (fill color, border). This json document also encodes the animation which is just how the bones move in each frame. My code then renders this json document to a set of pixel art frames using my desired lighting settings and color palette. 

I intend to make this approach more generally available but for now it’s an internal tool. Chunkyard.net is the site where I’m building this

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: general image models mostly give blurry pixels that only look like pixel art at 16-50 px. pixellab is made for sprites so it's the better bet for that size

comments.author: Snownova
comments.body:
Its funny, I tried to use GPT to create pixel art buildings for my project, and the results were horrid (it did pretty good on the pixel art character portraits though). Then I asked Claude to try the buildings and it did amazing.

Later I wanted  to upscale my game to HD. I asked Claude to upscale its designs from 64x to 256x and the results were the most amateurish paint buildings I've ever seen. Yet when I asked ChatGPT to try, it made wonderfully detailed buildings. It only had trouble keeping the style, perspective and coloration consistent, which I had to use Claude to fix.

I'm almost tempted to thrown a third model into the mix.

comments.author: Electronic-Movie4208
comments.body: I've been working on my own RPG, Lanternwake, using AI. 😄 ChatGPT's image generation is pretty good for creating pixel art concepts, but at 16–50 pixels, you'll probably need to clean things up manually in Aseprite or Piskel to get crisp results.

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: at 16-50 pixels, fixing the silhouette by hand can make a bigger difference than changing models
